newsitem.title: UK: Med Aframax rates firm on tight June tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Med Aframax rates firm on tight June tonnage.

text.p: Mediterranean rates continued to firm on Wednesday on a lack of June tonnage in the 80,000 tonne (Aframax) market, brokers said.
Cross-Med Aframaxes climbed to W140 from W125 on Tuesday, with one vessel, the Armata, rumoured fixed as high as W160 Banias/Milazzo although this could not be confirmed.
"It's all due to tight tonnage in the remainder of June," an Italian broker said.
Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes, meanwhile, remained at a fairly firm W125, with up to W132.5 quoted for a modern ship to Denmark.
Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Singapore dipped to W65 from W67.5 on dwindling enquiry but voyages to Japan and South Korea were steady at W72.5.
The ultra-large (ULCC) market, which was dormant last week, has revived with the 350,000 tonne Tina fixed at W57.5 for NITC on a Kharg Island/Red Sea voyage after two or three deals done on Tuesday.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs were steady at W65, while 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) edged down to W87.5 from W90. "It's the usual -- too many ships, not enough cargoes," a U.S. broker said.
The Caribs/upcoast market remained flat in contrast to the volatility it showed earlier in the year, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W170 and 50,000 tonne gas oil stems at W195.
The European fuel oil market was extremely quiet with inter-UKC rates around W225 and cross-Med at about W190, brokers said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
